first.rationale: I intend to run a small, guarded onboarding simplification test because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence links shorter onboarding and simpler signup to improved adoption. I would verify memory_86 as the most consequential direct precedent and memory_73 to assess whether targeted pricing is a stronger response to the competitor threat before ruling it out. The test should monitor qualified activation and downstream revenue quality, not just completion rates.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding, addressing both the 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline. The verified shortened-onboarding record showed +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention; signup simplification also previously improved SMB activation. Do not prioritize promotional pricing: although it increased signup and short-term qualified revenue, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to sustain through renewal. Track qualified activation, time-to-value, 30-day retention, and downstream qualified revenue to guard against optimizing completion alone.

final2.rationale: Proceed with the onboarding simplification experiment rather than reacting with broad discounting. It directly addresses the simultaneous declines in onboarding completion and activation, and the verified record showed higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention. The verified pricing test produced short-term acquisition and revenue lift but materially worse retention and failure through renewal, making deeper discounting a poor sustainable-revenue response despite the competitor's escalation. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn and qualified revenue as guardrails; this experiment may not fully resolve immediate price objections, but it avoids trading renewal economics for fragile acquisition.
